cards.title: Admission and scheduling
items: Invalid requests are rejected before a job exists. Valid submissions return HTTP 202 with a queued job and Location header.
All opened libraries share the server's write gate and collection semaphore. Queued writers cannot be starved by newly arriving collection readers.
Read jobs may overlap each other and staging or tool writes. Backup, export, and auto_install requests also take the write gate.

cards.title: Cancellation is cooperative
items: POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel cancels the job context and returns HTTP 202 with its current state; it does not immediately set cancelled.
A running operation that returns no error still succeeds even if cancellation raced with completion. An error with a cancelled context produces cancelled.
The scheduler observes cancellation while waiting. Shutdown cancels jobs and waits for workers. Retrying creates a new job; terminal jobs never return to queued.

cards.title: Observation and retained results
items: Status and SSE remain available while collection access is blocked. Last-Event-ID resumes retained events; an expired cursor requires status refresh and a fresh stream.

Terminal status, result, history ID, and terminal event are published together under the server mutex. Validated suggestion batches update retained results before terminal completion. Failed or cancelled operations can retain partial results and an undo record.
The server retains at most 128 jobs and 1024 events per job. When capacity is reached, admission evicts an older terminal job or refuses the request; restarting the server loses job state.

cards.title: Metadata refresh partial outcomes
items: library.refresh stops on unexpected file inspection, database write, or folder scan errors. Stable library_refresh_stat_failed, library_refresh_write_failed, and library_refresh_scan_failed codes identify recovery guidance.
Cancellation and errors retain the report after track enumeration. updatedCount counts only saved updates; missing and unindexed counts can be incomplete. Initial failures can have no result.

Saved updates remain covered by the existing safety snapshot and history. Review partial counts and the undo record before retrying; no automatic retry or rollback is performed. Cobra prints incomplete counts and returns an error.

Absolute stored audio paths are inspected at their original location, including external drives; relative paths resolve from the absolute library directory. Stored paths are preserved. Only the library directory is scanned for unindexed audio; an external path on another volume is not part of that scan.
